Pesquera Santa Isla Files for Bankruptcy Amid Industry Headwinds in Peru

LIMA – Pesquera Santa Isla, a prominent player in Peru’s fisheries sector, has filed for bankruptcy protection as it struggles to manage mounting debts and declining revenues. The company, which operates several processing plants along the northern coast, initiated bankruptcy proceedings in the Lima Commercial Court on Tuesday, citing “severe liquidity constraints” following a prolonged period of weak catch volumes and falling prices for fishmeal and fish oil exports.

In a statement released by the company, CEO Ricardo Zúñiga said, “Despite our best efforts to restructure and streamline operations, the ongoing challenges in the fisheries market have left us with no viable alternative but to seek court protection. Our primary priority is to maintain core operations while we work with creditors and authorities on a sustainable path forward.”

Pesquera Santa Isla’s plants in Piura and Chimbote have significantly reduced processing activity in recent weeks, with some temporary layoffs reported among plant workers. The company’s vessel fleet remains in port as management reviews operational plans and evaluates asset sales to raise funds for debt service.

According to data from the National Fisheries Association, Santa Isla accounted for nearly 7% of Peru’s fishmeal production last year, making it a key contributor to the sector. Industry analysts warn that the bankruptcy could add pressure to an already fragile industry environment, as adverse oceanic conditions and strict quota policies continue to impact supply.

Jorge Villanueva, fisheries market analyst at Lima-based consultancy ProMar, commented, “Santa Isla’s insolvency reflects deep-rooted structural issues in the sector, including overcapacity and volatility in global demand. Other firms will be closely watching the proceedings to assess potential ripple effects.”

At press time, the court had not yet appointed an administrator, and negotiations with creditors were ongoing.
